import re


def parse_iso_duration(s: str) -> int:
    if not isinstance(s, str):
        raise ValueError("duration must be a string")

    match = re.fullmatch(
        r"P"
        r"(?:(?P<years>[0-9]+)Y)?"
        r"(?:(?P<months>[0-9]+)M)?"
        r"(?:(?P<days>[0-9]+)D)?"
        r"(?:T"
        r"(?:(?P<hours>[0-9]+)H)?"
        r"(?:(?P<minutes>[0-9]+)M)?"
        r"(?:(?P<seconds>[0-9]+)S)?"
        r")?",
        s,
    )

    if match is None:
        raise ValueError("invalid ISO 8601 duration")

    values = match.groupdict()

    # At least one component must be present.
    if not any(value is not None for value in values.values()):
        raise ValueError("duration must contain at least one component")

    # T is valid only when followed by at least one time component.
    if "T" in s and not any(
        values[name] is not None for name in ("hours", "minutes", "seconds")
    ):
        raise ValueError("T must be followed by a time component")

    return (
        int(values["years"] or 0) * 365 * 86400
        + int(values["months"] or 0) * 30 * 86400
        + int(values["days"] or 0) * 86400
        + int(values["hours"] or 0) * 3600
        + int(values["minutes"] or 0) * 60
        + int(values["seconds"] or 0)
    )
